classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied auxiliary cosine form and a shifted domain to reject a negative solution and include the next revolution; these are routine linked procedures.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}D\cos(x+\varphi)&=D\cos x\cos\varphi-D\sin x\sin\varphi\\D\cos\varphi&=1\\D\sin\varphi&=3\\D^2(\cos^2\varphi+\sin^2\varphi)&=1^2+3^2\\D^2&=10\\D&=\sqrt{10}\quad(D>0)\\\tan\varphi&=\frac{D\sin\varphi}{D\cos\varphi}=3\\\varphi&=\tan^{-1}3\end{aligned}$$
Both $\sin\varphi$ and $\cos\varphi$ are positive, so $\varphi$ is in quadrant I.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence solve $\cos x-3\sin x=3$, for $0^\circ\leq x\leq360^\circ$. Give the solutions correct to the nearest minute where necessary.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sqrt{10}\cos(x+\varphi)&=3\\\cos(x+\varphi)&=\frac3{\sqrt{10}}\\\varphi&=\tan^{-1}3\approx71^\circ34'\end{aligned}$$
Let $\beta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac3{\sqrt{10}}\right)=90^\circ-\varphi\approx18^\circ26'$. The transformed domain is $\varphi\leq x+\varphi\leq360^\circ+\varphi$.
The candidate angles, including the extra revolution, are
$$\begin{aligned}x+\varphi&=\beta,\ 360^\circ-\beta,\ 360^\circ+\beta\\x&=90^\circ-2\varphi,\ 270^\circ,\ 450^\circ-2\varphi\end{aligned}$$
The first candidate is approximately $-53^\circ8'$ and is rejected. Thus $x=270^\circ$ or $x\approx306^\circ52'$.
